input.quote: Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
input.rationale: No provision anywhere in the Agreement requires Customer to pay liquidated damages, a penalty, an early-termination fee, or a minimum fee on termination. Searches for liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated/pre-estimated sums, forfeiture, acceleration, and termination-fee mechanics returned nothing payable by Customer: the only "penalty" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due; § 21.3 treats undisputed Fees for conforming Services as a payment obligation rather than damages; and § 22.2 addresses only actual audit costs and an undisputed usage shortfall. The Agreement therefore already sits at the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties. The § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment (USD 2,000,000 per year "without reduction or termination rights") is commercially similar exposure but is a minimum-volume commitment addressed under the minimum-commitment rule, so we do not flag it a second time here.
